questions.question_text:
Write the equation of the line shown, in the form $y=mx+c$.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6.2cm,height=6.2cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3,xmax=4,ymin=-5,ymax=7,xtick={-3,-2,...,4},ytick={-5,-4,...,7},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-2:2,samples=2] {3*x+1};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,1) (1,4)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Swapped the roles: read the y-intercept as the gradient and the gradient as the intercept.
Took the y-intercept as -1 instead of +1 where the line crosses the y-axis.
Computed run over rise instead of rise over run for the gradient.
